INPUTS & ISSUE TIME

What this prediction means.

Today’s complete daily inputs are provider estimates and include forecasts for hours that have not happened yet. AirCast then predicts the next calendar day. This hybrid live mode has not been prospectively validated. Historical 2025 scores describe the retrospective experiment, not proven accuracy for this live pipeline.

Frozen models trained during the hackathon on historical 2023–2025 data. CAMS is gridded atmospheric modelling; weather is a different input product from the historical reanalysis used in evaluation. Source changes and extreme events may reduce accuracy. No live prediction interval is claimed.

THE THINKING BEHIND AIRCAST

Local by design.
Transparent by default.

A Jaipur experiment in next-day air quality prediction.

01 / THE PEOPLE

For the plans we make outdoors.

AirCast helps Jaipur residents explore tomorrow’s fine-particle pollution before planning outdoor activities. School sports scheduling is one concrete use case. This prototype has not been user-tested.

Our addition to the hackathon baseline: a Jaipur-specific setting, honest historical replay, adjustable warning thresholds, uncertainty intervals, and a close look at missed warnings.

02 / THE DATA

Real archives. Clear limits.

Hourly PM₂.₅ estimates from Open-Meteo’s CAMS air-quality service, paired with Open-Meteo historical weather for Jaipur, 2023–2025. These are gridded model estimates and reanalysis, not CPCB station measurements.

Local-day means require at least 18 valid hours per variable; rainfall is summed. Missing days stay in the calendar. We do not fill gaps using future data.

03 / THE EXPERIMENT

Tomorrow stays out of training.

Features: today’s PM₂.₅, two daily lags, 3- and 7-day trailing means, temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind, pressure, and seasonal sine/cosine. Forecasts are issued after the origin day ends.

Train through June 2024; choose between a fixed ridge regression and random forest using July–December 2024 MAE. Freeze both, then evaluate January–December 2025 once. No random time split.

04 / THE LIMITS

A useful starting point.

Learning from CAMS partly measures how predictable another model’s estimates are. It does not demonstrate accuracy against ground truth. Revised weather reanalysis also differs from what was available in real time.

Daily averages miss hourly spikes. Dust events and emissions are not direct inputs. Intervals use validation residuals; coverage can shift. Next: validate on Jaipur CPCB sensors and run a prospective trial.

Sources & credits

Open-Meteo Air Quality API / CAMS ↗ · Open-Meteo Historical Weather API ↗ · CPCB: About the National AQI ↗

Open-Meteo data: CC BY 4.0. Contains modified Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service information. Models use scikit-learn, pandas and NumPy. Built with assistance from OpenAI Codex; team members must understand, review and credit the work.

India PM₂.₅ sub-index uses linear interpolation between CPCB breakpoints. For concentrations above 250 µg/m³, show “Severe” without inventing an upper breakpoint. An official AQI requires other pollutants and monitoring criteria.
